# Results

## Two distinct atrophy topographies

```{r fig1, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%", fig.cap = "**Figure 1. Atrophy topographies.** Group-level DBM atrophy (−t) on the cortex (Schaefer-400, warped to the template of the maps) and in 14 subcortical structures. Colour scale set per syndrome from the cortex; subcortical boxes print their values. *Caudate is dominated by DBM ventricular expansion."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(root, "figures/v2/web/fig1_atrophy.jpg"), rel_path = FALSE)
```

AD and MCI atrophy involved the medial temporal lobe, the posterior cingulate/precuneus and
lateral temporoparietal cortex; in the subcortex the amygdala was the most affected structure
(AD: `r f2(res$epicentres$sub414 %>% filter(syndrome == "AD", label == "Lamyg") %>% pull(atrophy))`
left, `r f2(res$epicentres$sub414 %>% filter(syndrome == "AD", label == "Ramyg") %>% pull(atrophy))`
right), followed by the thalamus and hippocampus. bvFTD involved orbitofrontal, anterior
insular, anterior cingulate and dorsomedial prefrontal cortex with diffuse striatal and
thalamic involvement; svPPA the anterior temporal lobe and nfvPPA the posterior frontal,
opercular and supplementary motor cortex (Figure 1). AD and bvFTD maps were only moderately
similar (r = `r f2(res$similarity$sub414 %>% filter(map1 == "AD", map2 == "bvFTD") %>% pull(r))`),
whereas AD and MCI were strongly similar (r = `r f2(res$similarity$sub414 %>% filter(map1 == "AD", map2 == "MCI") %>% pull(r))`;
Supplementary Table S5).

**Asymmetry.** Comparing each left region with the identical mirrored right region, AD, MCI
and bvFTD were symmetric (proportion of the most atrophic locations that were left-dominant:
AD `r f2(res$asymmetry %>% filter(syndrome == "AD") %>% pull(top20_left_greater))`, bvFTD
`r f2(res$asymmetry %>% filter(syndrome == "bvFTD") %>% pull(top20_left_greater))`; sign tests
p `r fp(res$asymmetry %>% filter(syndrome == "AD") %>% pull(sign_test_p))` and
p `r fp(res$asymmetry %>% filter(syndrome == "bvFTD") %>% pull(sign_test_p))`), whereas svPPA
(`r f2(res$asymmetry %>% filter(syndrome == "svPPA") %>% pull(top20_left_greater))`, p
`r fp(res$asymmetry %>% filter(syndrome == "svPPA") %>% pull(sign_test_p))`) and nfvPPA
(`r f2(res$asymmetry %>% filter(syndrome == "nfvPPA") %>% pull(top20_left_greater))`, p
`r fp(res$asymmetry %>% filter(syndrome == "nfvPPA") %>% pull(sign_test_p))`) were
left-lateralised. The left-dominant anterior insula seen in the raw bvFTD parcellation arises
in two steps: Schaefer's left and right ventral prefrontal/insular parcels differ in size and
position, so the raw left parcel is more atrophic than the raw right parcel; but when the same
left parcel samples the mirrored map, its value does not drop, so the difference is not a
hemispheric difference in the disease (Supplementary Figure S2).

## Atrophy is organised along the cortical sheet

```{r fig2, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 9.5, fig.height = 6.4, fig.cap = "**Figure 2. Predicting each region's atrophy from all other regions (Schaefer-400 cortex).** Dots: r(atrophy, prediction). Filled dots: significant against the variogram-matched null (FDR q < 0.05, r > 0). Grey bars: central 95% of the variogram null for each model (parameters refitted). The two spatial baselines (bottom) use Euclidean or geodesic distance; network models use the structural (SC) or functional (FC) connectome."}
E_models <- c("SC_direct", "SPE", "communicability", "search_prob", "navigation", "heat", "FC", "FC_top10", "distance")
mk <- function(cfg) res$models[[cfg]] %>% filter(R == 0, model %in% E_models) %>% mutate(config = cfg)
d2 <- bind_rows(mk("ctx400_euc"), mk("ctx400_geo") %>% filter(model == "distance") %>% mutate(model = "distance_geo"))
band <- function(cfg, ms, rename = NULL) {
  nl <- readRDS(file.path(root, sprintf("output/cache_v2/null_variogram_%s.rds", cfg)))$fits
  b <- nl %>% filter(R == 0, model %in% ms) %>% group_by(model, syndrome) %>% summarise(lo = quantile(r, .025, na.rm = TRUE), hi = quantile(r, .975, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  if (!is.null(rename)) b$model <- rename
  b
}
bb <- bind_rows(band("ctx400_euc", E_models), band("ctx400_geo", "distance", "distance_geo"))
d2 <- d2 %>% left_join(bb, by = c("model", "syndrome")) %>%
  mutate(sig = ifelse(!is.na(q_variogram) & q_variogram < 0.05 & r > 0, "q < 0.05", "n.s."),
         model = factor(model_lab[model], rev(model_lab[c(E_models[-length(E_models)], "distance", "distance_geo")])),
         syndrome = factor(syndrome, syn_order))
ggplot(d2, aes(r, model)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "#a8a79f", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), height = 0, colour = "#d6d5ce", linewidth = 2.4) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = sig), colour = pal[["blue"]], fill = pal[["bg"]], size = 2.3, stroke = 0.9) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("q < 0.05" = 16, "n.s." = 21), name = "Variogram null") +
  facet_wrap(~syndrome, ncol = 3) + scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 0.4, 0.8)) +
  labs(x = "r(atrophy, predicted atrophy)", y = NULL) + theme_ms
```

A purely spatial kernel predicted each region's atrophy from the atrophy of other regions
better than any network model in every syndrome (Figure 2). The geodesic kernel performed
better than the Euclidean kernel (AD r = `r f2(rv("ctx400_geo", 0, "distance", "AD"))` vs
`r f2(rv("ctx400_euc", 0, "distance", "AD"))`; bvFTD `r f2(rv("ctx400_geo", 0, "distance", "bvFTD"))`
vs `r f2(rv("ctx400_euc", 0, "distance", "bvFTD"))`; svPPA `r f2(rv("ctx400_geo", 0, "distance", "svPPA"))`
vs `r f2(rv("ctx400_euc", 0, "distance", "svPPA"))`), with fitted length scales of
`r f2(min(mrow("ctx400_geo", 0, "distance", "AD")$param, mrow("ctx400_geo", 0, "distance", "bvFTD")$param))`–`r f2(max(res$models$ctx400_geo %>% filter(R == 0, model == "distance") %>% pull(param)))` mm.
Thus Euclidean distance does not inflate the spatial baseline by bridging sulci; proximity
along the cortex is the better description. The geodesic kernel also exceeded the surrogates
of the variogram null, which preserve Euclidean autocorrelation, in AD
(p `r fp(pv("ctx400_geo", 0, "distance", "AD"))`), bvFTD (p `r fp(pv("ctx400_geo", 0, "distance", "bvFTD"))`)
and svPPA (p `r fp(pv("ctx400_geo", 0, "distance", "svPPA"))`).

## Structural communication models add little beyond geometry

Direct SC, shortest-path efficiency, communicability, search information, navigation and
the network diffusion kernel all predicted atrophy (e.g. AD search information
r = `r f2(rv("ctx400_euc", 0, "search_prob", "AD"))`; bvFTD
r = `r f2(rv("ctx400_euc", 0, "search_prob", "bvFTD"))`), and these fits were significant
against spins and degree-preserving rewiring. None was significant against the
variogram-matched null in any syndrome, and none exceeded the distance baseline (Figure 2;
Supplementary Table S6). Against geometry-preserving rewiring, only bvFTD retained an
effect for path-based models (shortest-path efficiency q `r fp(qv("ctx400_euc", 0, "SPE", "bvFTD", "rew_geo"))`;
navigation q `r fp(qv("ctx400_euc", 0, "navigation", "bvFTD", "rew_geo"))`), and this depended on the
bin width of the null: it held with 5–20 edge-length bins but not with 40 (Supplementary
Table S9b). Giving each
communication model the same single fitted parameter as the distance kernel produced at
most ties with distance (Supplementary Table S7). Diffusion efficiency (1/mean first-passage
time) is dominated by node strength on graphs of this size [16] and gave negative or
near-zero fits; the network diffusion kernel's best fit collapsed to one step (β at the low
end of its range).

## A long-range functional component specific to frontotemporal dementia

```{r fig3, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 9.5, fig.height = 4.2, fig.cap = "**Figure 3. Distance-censored prediction.** Each model may use only regions further than R mm (Euclidean) from the target. Lines: r(atrophy, prediction) at each radius. Dashed: 95th percentile of the variogram null for thresholded FC (top 10%)."}
cm <- c("SC_direct", "search_prob", "heat", "FC_top10", "distance")
d3 <- bind_rows(res$models$ctx400_euc %>% filter(model %in% cm), res$models$ctx400_geo %>% filter(model == "distance") %>% mutate(model = "distance_geo")) %>%
  filter(syndrome %in% c("AD", "MCI", "bvFTD", "svPPA", "nfvPPA")) %>%
  mutate(model = factor(model_lab[model], model_lab[c(cm, "distance_geo")]), syndrome = factor(syndrome, syn_order))
nlv <- readRDS(file.path(root, "output/cache_v2/null_variogram_ctx400_euc.rds"))$fits %>% filter(model == "FC_top10") %>%
  group_by(R, syndrome) %>% summarise(hi = quantile(r, .95, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>% filter(syndrome %in% levels(d3$syndrome)) %>%
  mutate(syndrome = factor(syndrome, syn_order))
cols3 <- setNames(c(pal[["blue"]], pal[["aqua"]], pal[["violet"]], pal[["orange"]], pal[["muted"]], pal[["ink"]]), model_lab[c(cm, "distance_geo")])
ggplot(d3, aes(R, r, colour = model)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "#a8a79f", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line(data = nlv, aes(R, hi), inherit.aes = FALSE, linetype = 2, colour = pal[["orange"]], linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) + geom_point(size = 1.3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cols3, name = NULL) + facet_wrap(~syndrome, nrow = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 30, 60)) +
  labs(x = "Exclusion radius R (mm)", y = "r") + theme_ms + guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 1))
```

When nearby regions were excluded, the picture separated by disease (Figure 3). With only
regions more than 30 mm away, thresholded FC predicted bvFTD atrophy at
r = `r f2(rv("ctx400_euc", 30, "FC_top10", "bvFTD"))` and pooled FTD at
r = `r f2(rv("ctx400_euc", 30, "FC_top10", "FTD"))` (variogram q
`r fp(qv("ctx400_euc", 30, "FC_top10", "bvFTD"))` and `r fp(qv("ctx400_euc", 30, "FC_top10", "FTD"))`;
also significant against spins and Moran surrogates), far above both distance kernels
(bvFTD geodesic r = `r f2(rv("ctx400_geo", 30, "distance", "bvFTD"))`). The corresponding
values were r = `r f2(rv("ctx400_euc", 30, "FC_top10", "svPPA"))` in svPPA and
`r f2(rv("ctx400_euc", 30, "FC_top10", "nfvPPA"))` in nfvPPA, but only
`r f2(rv("ctx400_euc", 30, "FC_top10", "AD"))` in AD and
`r f2(rv("ctx400_euc", 30, "FC_top10", "MCI"))` in MCI. Beyond distance, FC added a unique
contribution in bvFTD (partial r = `r f2(part("ctx400_geo", 30, "FC_top10", "bvFTD")$partial_r)`,
variogram p `r fp(part("ctx400_geo", 30, "FC_top10", "bvFTD")$p_variogram)`) and pooled FTD
(`r f2(part("ctx400_geo", 30, "FC_top10", "FTD")$partial_r)`) that was about half as large in AD
(`r f2(part("ctx400_geo", 30, "FC_top10", "AD")$partial_r)`, variogram p
`r fp(part("ctx400_geo", 30, "FC_top10", "AD")$p_variogram)`) and smaller still in MCI
(`r f2(part("ctx400_geo", 30, "FC_top10", "MCI")$partial_r)`; Supplementary Table S8).
Among structural models only bvFTD retained a smaller long-range contribution beyond
distance (search information partial r = `r f2(part("ctx400_geo", 30, "search_prob", "bvFTD")$partial_r)`,
variogram q `r fp(part("ctx400_geo", 30, "search_prob", "bvFTD")$q_variogram)`). Full-density
FC behaved like thresholded FC but weaker (bvFTD r = `r f2(rv("ctx400_euc", 30, "FC", "bvFTD"))`).

## Generative spreading: no advantage for the structural connectome

```{r fig4, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 9.5, fig.height = 3.6, fig.cap = "**Figure 4. Generative models seeded at the best node (or bilateral pair).** Network diffusion on the SC or FC versus isotropic spatial spread (Euclidean or geodesic) from the seed, cortex only (left) and with subcortex (right). Seed and parameter refitted in every null surrogate."}
gm <- bind_rows(res$generative$ctx400_geo$fits %>% mutate(space = "Cortex (400)"), res$generative$sub414_euc$fits %>% mutate(space = "Cortex + subcortex (414)")) %>%
  mutate(model = recode(model, NDM_SC = "Network diffusion (SC)", NDM_FC = "Network diffusion (FC)", spread_euclid = "Spatial spread (Euclidean)", spread_geodesic = "Spatial spread (geodesic)"),
         syndrome = factor(syndrome, syn_order))
cols4 <- c("Network diffusion (SC)" = pal[["blue"]], "Network diffusion (FC)" = pal[["orange"]], "Spatial spread (Euclidean)" = pal[["muted"]], "Spatial spread (geodesic)" = pal[["ink"]])
ggplot(gm, aes(syndrome, r, colour = model)) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.6), size = 2.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cols4, name = NULL) + facet_wrap(~space) + ylim(0, 0.8) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "r(atrophy, generated map)") + theme_ms + guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 1))
```

Seeded network diffusion on the SC was never better than isotropic spatial spread from the
same seed (Figure 4). In AD, the best cortical seeds were bilateral anterior/medial temporal
parcels, and geodesic spread from them explained the map better than diffusion along the SC
(r = `r f2(gen("ctx400_geo", "spread_geodesic", "AD")$r)` vs
`r f2(gen("ctx400_geo", "NDM_SC", "AD")$r)`; difference variogram p
`r fp(gdiff("ctx400_geo", "NDM_SC", "spread_geodesic", "AD")$p_variogram)`). With the subcortex
included, every model chose the bilateral amygdala as the AD seed, and SC diffusion
(r = `r f2(gen("sub414_euc", "NDM_SC", "AD")$r)`) and spatial spread
(r = `r f2(gen("sub414_euc", "spread_euclid", "AD")$r)`) were indistinguishable. In bvFTD, SC
diffusion from a left ventrolateral prefrontal seed and spatial spread performed equally
(r = `r f2(gen("ctx400_geo", "NDM_SC", "bvFTD")$r)` and `r f2(gen("ctx400_geo", "spread_geodesic", "bvFTD")$r)`).
FC-based diffusion from a single seed performed poorly in every syndrome, in contrast to the
static FC-neighbour models above: the FC signal in FTD reflects the distributed functional
network rather than spread from one focus.

## Adding the subcortex does not rescue the structural connectome in AD

With 14 subcortical structures added (414 nodes), the structural models still failed the
variogram null in AD (search information r = `r f2(rv("sub414_euc", 0, "search_prob", "AD"))`,
p `r fp(pv("sub414_euc", 0, "search_prob", "AD"))`) and carried no long-range signal
(R = 30 mm: r = `r f2(rv("sub414_euc", 30, "search_prob", "AD"))`). Thresholded FC gained a
modest long-range contribution in AD (r = `r f2(rv("sub414_euc", 30, "FC_top10", "AD"))`,
variogram p `r fp(pv("sub414_euc", 30, "FC_top10", "AD"))`), still well below bvFTD
(r = `r f2(rv("sub414_euc", 30, "FC_top10", "bvFTD"))`) and pooled FTD
(r = `r f2(rv("sub414_euc", 30, "FC_top10", "FTD"))`).

## Functional hubs and signal dropout

```{r hubs, echo = FALSE}
hb <- res$hubs$ctx400 %>% filter(strength %in% c("FC", "FC_top10"), syndrome %in% syn_order) %>%
  transmute(Strength = recode(strength, FC = "FC (full)", FC_top10 = "FC (top 10%)"), Syndrome = factor(syndrome, syn_order),
            rho = f2(rho), `p (spin)` = fp(p_spin), `rho | EPI signal` = f2(rho_partial_epi), `p (spin) | EPI` = fp(p_spin_partial),
            `rho(strength, EPI)` = f2(rho_strength_epi)) %>% arrange(Strength, Syndrome)
knitr::kable(hb, caption = "**Table 1. FC node strength and atrophy (Spearman), raw and controlling for regional EPI signal (dropout proxy).** Schaefer-400 cortex; p from 1,000 spins.")
```

Regions with high FC strength were less atrophic in bvFTD and pooled FTD, with full-density
and with thresholded FC (Table 1), whereas SC strength was weakly positively related to
bvFTD atrophy (ρ = `r f2(res$hubs$ctx400 %>% filter(strength == "SC", syndrome == "bvFTD") %>% pull(rho))`).
Regional EPI signal, our proxy for susceptibility dropout, was lowest in orbitofrontal and
anterior temporal cortex (limbic network `r f2(res$epi_by_network %>% filter(network == "Limbic") %>% pull(epi_signal))`
of the cortical median), but it was only weakly related to FC strength
(ρ = `r f2(res$hubs$ctx400 %>% filter(strength == "FC", syndrome == "AD") %>% pull(rho_strength_epi))`),
and partialling it out left the bvFTD association unchanged
(ρ = `r f2(res$hubs$ctx400 %>% filter(strength == "FC", syndrome == "bvFTD") %>% pull(rho))` →
`r f2(res$hubs$ctx400 %>% filter(strength == "FC", syndrome == "bvFTD") %>% pull(rho_partial_epi))`).
This proxy, a template from a different scanner and sequence, cannot exclude HCP-specific
dropout, and low FC strength is also a known property of limbic and orbitofrontal networks.
We therefore report the association without interpreting it as sparing of functional hubs.

## The choice of null model decides significance

```{r fig5, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 9.5, fig.height = 3.4, fig.cap = "**Figure 5. Number of model fits with a positive network constraint (r > 0, FDR q < 0.05) under each null.** Schaefer-400 cortex; SC models (direct, shortest-path, communicability, search information, navigation, diffusion kernel) and thresholded FC, six syndromes, at R = 0 and 30 mm."}
nm5 <- c("SC_direct", "SPE", "communicability", "search_prob", "navigation", "heat", "FC_top10")
d5 <- res$models$ctx400_euc %>% filter(R %in% c(0, 30), model %in% nm5) %>%
  select(R, model, syndrome, starts_with("supported_")) %>% pivot_longer(starts_with("supported_"), names_to = "null", values_to = "ok") %>%
  mutate(null = recode(sub("supported_", "", null), spin = "Spin", variogram = "Variogram", moran = "Moran", rew_deg = "Rewired (degree)", rew_geo = "Rewired (degree + geometry)"),
         family = ifelse(model == "FC_top10", "FC (top 10%)", "SC models")) %>%
  filter(!(family == "FC (top 10%)" & grepl("Rewired", null))) %>%
  group_by(R, family, null) %>% summarise(n_ok = sum(ok), n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(null = factor(null, c("Spin", "Variogram", "Moran", "Rewired (degree)", "Rewired (degree + geometry)")), Rl = paste0("R = ", R, " mm"))
ggplot(d5, aes(n_ok / n, null, fill = family)) + geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(n_ok, "/", n)), position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), hjust = -0.15, size = 2.8, colour = pal[["ink"]]) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("SC models" = pal[["blue"]], "FC (top 10%)" = pal[["orange"]]), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1.15), breaks = c(0, .5, 1)) +
  facet_wrap(~Rl) + labs(x = "Share of fits supported", y = NULL) + theme_ms
```

Whether a structural model appeared to constrain atrophy depended mostly on the null
(Figure 5). Degree-preserving rewiring supported almost every structural fit, because it
roughly doubles the mean connection length and so destroys the spatial embedding that the
real connectome shares with atrophy. Spins supported about a third of structural fits at
R = 0, because parcel-level spins make surrogate maps rougher at short range than the real map (short-range variogram ratio
`r f2(min(res$null_diag %>% filter(null == "spin") %>% pull(variogram_ratio_bins1to5)))`–`r f2(max(res$null_diag %>% filter(null == "spin") %>% pull(variogram_ratio_bins1to5)))`
times the empirical value, vs `r f2(min(res$null_diag %>% filter(null == "moran") %>% pull(variogram_ratio_bins1to5)))`–`r f2(max(res$null_diag %>% filter(null == "moran") %>% pull(variogram_ratio_bins1to5)))`
for Moran surrogates, which are slightly smoother than the real maps; Supplementary
Table S9). Variogram-matched surrogates supported no structural fit and geometry-preserving
rewiring very few, whereas the thresholded-FC result in bvFTD and FTD survived every spatial
null.

## Eigenmodes within each hemisphere

```{r eig, echo = FALSE}
eg <- res$eigen %>% filter(K %in% c(10, 20)) %>% group_by(syndrome, basis, K) %>% summarise(r = mean(r), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = basis, values_from = r) %>% mutate(syndrome = factor(syndrome, syn_order)) %>% arrange(K, syndrome) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric) & !K, f2))
knitr::kable(eg, caption = "**Table 2. Reconstruction of atrophy from the first K eigenmodes, computed within each hemisphere** (mean r of the two hemispheres). Geometric = Laplace–Beltrami modes of the hemisphere's cortical surface; SC/FC = harmonics of that hemisphere's SC or FC graph.")
```

When all bases were computed within each hemisphere, geometric eigenmodes reconstructed AD
and MCI atrophy at least as well as connectome harmonics, whereas FC harmonics reconstructed
bvFTD best at low K (Table 2), in line with the static and censored analyses.

## Robustness

The main results were unchanged at 200 and 100 parcels (Supplementary Table S10): no
structural model exceeded the distance baseline, and the long-range FC effect in bvFTD and
pooled FTD remained significant against the variogram null.
